Sara — thanks for the flag and logs. We're treating this as a P0. Initial triage shows an amplification pattern consistent with recent model variant rollout in us-east1 AZ3: KV-cache thrashing + a hot prefix causing persistent prefix misses -> request amplification and queue accumulation on the AZ3 serving mesh. We're seeing backend worker saturation and 502s as requests time out waiting for cache rebuilds.

Immediate mitigation options (recommendation in bold):
- Option A: Cross-region evacuation of ClearBay traffic from us-east1 AZ3 -> us-east2 (preferred) with temporary priority pin + canary rollout on east2. This buys headroom and reduces queue pressure in AZ3. Requires exec sign-off for elevated priority and short-term capacity bump.
- Option B: Emergency per-customer circuit breaker in AZ3 (throttle + degrade to smaller model variant) — lower blast radius but customer-visible quality drop.
- Option C: Revert recent model variant in AZ3 (risky if rollout completes during rollback window).

Requesting:
1) Exec approval to move forward with Option A (regional reroute + elevated priority for ClearBay for 2–4 hrs).
2) Engineering runbook execution (Hannah / Markus to coordinate drain + KV warmup plan).
3) Communication copy for ClearBay and downstream customers (Jordan).

I will start a limited canary on us-east2 if we get sign-off. Attaching kvcache diagnostics we pulled.

Attachments: kvcache-diagnostics-20260721.tar.gz

-Neha
